scope: Named 6/7/24/29/43-coordinate profiles, FK, bounded IK, URDF fixed transforms and rejection of unsupported joints
Integrated simulation and fake-SDK G2/G1/Dex3 driver behavior, read-only publishers and feedback races
Arming, held enable, ownership, input ordering, transport TTL, hold/re-anchor and latched software stop
Hold failure revokes ownership; stale feedback, rejected commands and slow IK cannot continue normal dispatch
Asynchronous recording, dimensions, queue overflow, incomplete episodes and tamper detection
Real loopback HTTP authentication, origin checks, typed errors, recorded-camera hash checks and display-only replay
Actual app.js input logic in a Node VM: focus, visibility, zero trigger and frozen XR expiry
Real synthetic JPEG persistence and MP4 decoding/export without opening a camera

limitations: G2/G1 drivers were verified against official interfaces and fake SDK contracts, not physical robots or target SDK/firmware environments.
Bundled geometry and limits are demonstrations; physical execution requires accurate models, site configuration and hardware acceptance.
No physical gamepad or AR/XR headset was tested. HTTP and isolated JavaScript tests cover UI behavior, but full visual browser acceptance has not been performed.
The generic guard covers joint limits, rates and freshness. G1 walking, collision planning and whole-body balance are outside this implementation.
The Python/HTTP runtime is neither hard-real-time nor functionally safety-certified; firmware protection and stop behavior require site verification.
Hands support grasp synergy and named joint targets, without generic independent-finger IK.
